findings.text: Provides typed copy-in from user memory for IOMMU control structures with single object, indexed array element and whole array forms. The single and indexed forms derive expected kernel size and required prefix length from the destination type and a named final mandatory member, then delegate to a shared validator. The indexed form checks the array descriptor and synthesizes one element descriptor by scaling the per entry stride. The whole array form requires matching type codes and a non empty count, performs one bulk transfer when host stride equals caller stride, and otherwise copies element by element with per element length negotiation.

Provides typed copy-out toward user memory for IOMMU control structures. A convenience wrapper derives kernel object size and required prefix length from the source type and a named final mandatory member, then delegates to a shared routine. The shared routine rejects absent descriptors, requires matching type codes, requires the user buffer to cover the mandatory prefix and the kernel object to cover the user length, then performs length negotiated transfer with trailing handling.

Copy helpers enforce a uniform validation contract. Type codes must equal the expected operation code. User length must cover the mandatory prefix and kernel length must cover the user length on output. Array descriptors must be present with non zero entry count and the requested index must lie strictly below the count. Null descriptors and out of range indices follow a warned invalid argument path.

Defines interoperable structure copy toward user space with version tolerance. The transfer length is the smaller of kernel and user sizes and the size difference is treated as trailing bytes. Oversized kernel input relative to its known object bound is rejected as too large. When the user buffer is larger the excess tail is zero filled, and an optional flag reports whether a smaller user buffer truncated non zero kernel tail bytes. Access failures report memory fault and success reports zero.

Driver dispatch table for IOMMU instances. It groups capability and hardware description queries, several paging and identity and shared address and nested domain constructors with device and flag and user data context, device lifecycle hooks for probing and releasing and finalizing and grouping, reserved region enumeration, firmware translation and deferred attach queries, per device fault response and default domain type selection, virtualized IOMMU sizing and initialization, plus a default domain operations pointer, module ownership, preallocated identity and blocked and release and default domains, and a single bit user PASID table capability.

Per domain operation table. It covers device attachment and PASID attachment with previous domain context, page mapping and unmapping with address and physical backing and granularity and count and protection and allocation context and progress reporting, full invalidation and range synchronized invalidation with gather context, user requested cache invalidation over an array descriptor, translation from I/O virtual address to physical, cache coherency enforcement query, page table quirk programming, and domain destruction.

Device side IOMMU bookkeeping. An IOMMU instance record links into a global list, references its driver operations and firmware node and hardware device, optionally holds a singleton group, advertises a maximum PASID count and a readiness flag. A per device record serializes access, holds a protected fault parameter pointer, firmware specification, back pointer to the managing IOMMU, opaque driver private data, PASID limit, and single bit deferred attach and PCI workaround and direct mapping and flush shadowing flags. A firmware specification record holds its firmware node, flag word, identifier count and trailing identifier array.

Fault and attachment state. A fault parameter block serializes queue management, tracks users by reference count with deferred reclamation, associates a device and queue and queue list, and maintains pending partial and complete fault lists. An attach handle binds an attachment to its domain. A shared address attachment extends that handle with its device and user count. A memory descriptor record carries a PASID, address space pointer, list of associated shared domains and list linkage for address space tracking.

Active translation cache maintenance path. Initialization resets a gather context to an empty interval with maximum start and an empty page list. Range addition widens the tracked interval to cover the new extent. Disjointness testing reports whether a candidate extent lies outside the current interval with a guard gap. Page addition synchronizes when granularity changes or the new page is disjoint, then records granularity and widens the interval. Synchronization invokes the domain operation only when a non empty interval is pending and then reinitializes the context. Full flush invokes the domain full invalidate operation when present. A predicate reports queued mode. Paging domain allocation with default flags delegates to the flagged constructor, and IOMMU device lookup resolves the managing instance from device state or driver data with container based downcasting.

Dirty tracking helpers pair an address bitmap with an optional gather context. Initialization optionally resets the gather context and then binds both pointers into the dirty descriptor. Recording updates the bitmap interval when a bitmap is present and widens the gather interval when a gather context is present. The underlying bitmap set primitive observed here performs no action.

Small device accessors. One resolves the managing IOMMU instance from driver data. Firmware specification retrieval returns the attached specification when device IOMMU state exists and null otherwise, while assignment installs the caller provided specification into existing device state. Private data retrieval returns opaque driver data when device state exists and null otherwise.

Disabled build placeholder types. When the IOMMU API is unavailable the driver operations, group, firmware specification, device, fault parameter, gather context, dirty bitmap and dirty operations types collapse to empty definitions without members or behavior.

Disabled build core contract. Capability queries always report false. Paging domain constructors report missing device. Gather initialization and synchronization and page addition and dirty bitmap handling become silent no operations. Queued mode queries always report false.

Disabled build domain device and group operations uniformly signal absence or succeed silently. Domain freeing, device detachment, reservation fetching and release, default mode selection, group detachment, group data handling, device removal, group release, quirk handling and fault handler installation perform no action with success or null or zero results as appropriate. Domain allocation, device attachment, address mapping, scatter mapping, group reservation query, group allocation, group naming, group device addition, group iteration, group identifier query, group attachment and device registration report missing device. Address translation and unmapping report zero extent, lookups for domain by device and group by device and group data and driver data return null, and default passthrough query reports true.

Disabled build device infrastructure. Unregistration, sysfs removal, link removal and default domain release do nothing. Sysfs addition, firmware specification initialization and identifier addition report missing device. Device linking reports invalid argument. Firmware specification lookup returns null. Default domain acquisition reports success.

Disabled build ownership, PASID and reset contract. Group ownership claim, device ownership claim and PASID attachment report missing device, while releases and detachments do nothing. Ownership query reports unclaimed. Global PASID allocation returns the invalid PASID value and freeing does nothing. Reset preparation reports success and completion does nothing.

Miscellaneous active helpers. Interrupt address preparation, group mutex assertion and debugfs setup complete silently with success. Scatter table mapping delegates to scatter list mapping over the table extents with kernel allocation context. Cookie retrieval for message signaled interrupts reports missing device.

Firmware and platform ABI constants. One flag marks PCI root complex address translation service support at bit zero and another marks write back snoop capability at bit one of the firmware specification flag word. A Tegra stream identifier bypass value is defined as one hundred twenty seven.

Tegra stream identifier extraction succeeds only when the IOMMU API is enabled and the device carries a firmware specification with exactly one identifier. On success it returns the low sixteen bits of that identifier and signals success, otherwise it signals failure without modifying the output.

Synchronization and lifetime rules. Fault parameter blocks serialize queue and fault list access with a dedicated mutex, count users with a reference count and defer reclamation through RCU. Per device IOMMU state serializes firmware specification and fault parameter and private data linkage with its own mutex while the fault parameter pointer itself is RCU protected. Shared address attachments count users with a reference count.

Failure and diagnostic behavior. Null array or data pointers and out of range indices follow warned invalid argument paths. Mismatched type codes, empty arrays, undersized user buffers and oversized user lengths relative to kernel objects likewise report invalid argument. User memory access failures during bulk, element wise, clearing or interoperable copies report memory fault. Kernel object size exceeding its compile time known bound reports too large. Successful paths report zero.

Gather context lifecycle. A context begins empty after initialization, accumulates a contiguous interval and granularity as ranges arrive, transitions through synchronization that flushes the pending interval and returns to empty when a disjoint extent or granularity change arrives or when explicitly synchronized, and remains in queued versus direct mode as indicated by its flag.
External minimum helper owned by another dossier and relied upon for interoperable length selection.
External maximum helper owned by another dossier and relied upon for trailing length computation.
